An important section missing in many one-pagers

why now

lots of things are "problems"
lots of things are "good ideas"

but that doesn't mean you have do them now
I really believe companies need roles that report directly to the CEO, that don't have a functional hat in the game.  Their responsibility is the smooth functioning of the *whole*, not the parts.

If a team "scored" themselves on these weekly ... I wouldn't care one bit about "story points" or velocity.

Focus on inputs, and good things will follow.

Play the game well, and the "score will take care of itself".

fascinating quote from some research:

"It is amazing how quickly you lose your skills and instincts when you work in an environment where you have no time to think... it really hurt me when I tried to get my next job"
why did the product manager cross the road?

product management is 90% forecasting...

...forecasting whether anyone will read your doc

YAGNI
"You aren't gonna need it"

....is an important concept

but so is YAGFIL
"you're not going to fix it later"

basically, own up to the fact that even if you rationalize you're going to fix it later... you probably aren't going to

A reminder I have near my desk.

Product work involves making decisions.

Different types of decisions...

quote from a CTO

"If I'm honest with myself, I'm not really up on certain new ways of working. I get the theory. But it has been more than decade since I worked on a team. I recently took a full week off to be a member of one of our teams, and my god things are different"

"We're so busy! We don't have time to write one-pagers! Do you have something more lightweight?"

Grab a notecard my friend....

internal platform product management is an order of magnitude harder than customer-facing PdM (in my opinion)

...and in most/many cases there's an order of magnitude LESS support, training, care, and infrastructure/ops, and education to help those PMs

"overestimation"
